claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as lacking a tutorial or clear explanation of its mechanics and objectives, leaving players confused about what to do.

citations.review_text:
Everything you do in this game gets undone within not minutes, but seconds - and sometimes your choice to act buys you the smallest, useless bit of time before what you were trying to stop happens anyways. Game design is muddy and unclear and even when you do understand what you're supposed to do by the endgame it's completely impossible to make progress because your location is just magically known by everybody around you but your last goat is just completely missing. By the time a human being can react to the same scare flung at you 1000 times ad nauseum, it's already too late even if you were being OVERLY cautious. All this with terribly slow XP that gates you out of perks that might even help alleviate some of my issues for hours.

I get the point. There's even some interesting stuff here. But why is it like this?
Refunded the game. Nothing explained, clunky mechanics, atmosphere sucks. There are several games similar to this that do everything better.

I gave it a shot, but honestly… it just didn’t click for me. It’s got that co-op horror vibe, sure — creepy atmosphere, dark hallways, spooky sounds — but it never really managed to scare me or pull me in. We jumped in expecting some proper tension or clever scares, but instead it felt more like running in circles not quite knowing what we were supposed to be doing.

The concept seems fun — working together to banish demons and survive — but the execution just didn’t land for me. The gameplay loop felt confusing, the objectives weren’t clear, and after a while it just became more frustrating than frightening.

It’s not bad, it just didn’t give me the horror experience I was hoping for. After a few rounds I realized it wasn’t for me, so yeah — refunding this one. Maybe it’ll click better with hardcore co-op horror fans, but I’ll stick with something that actually gets my heart rate up. 👻💀

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players notice the core ritual loop turning familiar over time.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the core gameplay loop as collecting items, avoiding monsters, and completing rituals across different maps, noting that it can become familiar and repetitive over time.

citations.review_text:
[h1]Devour[/h1]

The game thrives on teamwork, tension, and unpredictability. Every playthrough randomly spawns items and locked doors, so no two runs feel exactly the same. You’ll be solving rituals, avoiding horrors, hiding in closets, and hoping that this time you don’t get snatched by Azazel’s minions.

[b]Why it’s fun:[/b]
• Co‑op chaos: Up to 4 players can join together, communicate with positional voice chat, and share both jump scares and laughs.
• Replayability: Randomized item spawns and escalating difficulty keep sessions fresh.
• Atmosphere: Creepy environments like a farmhouse, asylum, and manor create real tension as the demon hunts you.
• Progression system: Cult Rank and Ritual Tokens unlock perks that help make your next run easier… or at least more strategic.

[b]Some downsides:[/b]
• Can feel repetitive: The core loop (collect items, avoid monster, complete ritual) can get familiar after many sessions.
• Solo play is rough: Without friends or other players, the game can feel slower or frustrating.
• Horror fades over time: Jump scares and tension are great early, but some players feel they lose impact after several runs.
• Community lobbies vary: Public matches might be sparse at times, so playing with friends or finding a group can improve the experience.

[b]Final verdict:[/b]
A solid indie horror co‑op with jump scares, strategy, and enough chaos to keep friends screaming together. Worth it if you love multiplayer horror that’s unpredictable and fun.

Devour Game Review
(Disclaimer - This is just my opinion and may be unpopular or disliked. Also, game has elements of death, religion and cults so if you are sensitive to this it may not be a game for you.)

(General)
1. This is a co-op horror game, where you can play with up to 4 players including yourself.
2. The characters, locations, adds, and gameplay has different types of horror elements making it eerie and tense.

(Positive)
1. The playable cultist characters have diversity giving a decent amount of playable choices both male and female.
2. Not all cosmetic items have to be bought some can be collected throughout the maps by getting all of a certain collectable.
3. All the main antogonists per map have are unique and the concept art for them are done well. 
4. I enjoy that they tied this game to The Watchers through the first locations Antagonist as-well-as the content they chose to expand links to The Watchers.
5. Not to fan girl, but the Cowboy antagonist on the one map is really cool and his concept ,even though it is difficult as he has range, was just so cool that it was hard to get frustrated when being dropped.
6. The adds, also, had diversity and work put into them, which made them interesting.
7. The games non-playable characters and atmospehere really adde to the horror feel.
6. The game connects well with other players and doesn't drop connection while hosting, or being on the hosted server.

(Negative)
1. The game does become repetive and tedious even when playing co-op.
2. The game becomes tense rather than scary as the Antagonists can get frustarting, or you can get overpowered by adds and dropped due to the UV running out and not recharging fast enough  even with the perk.
3. For them being cultists, the storyline of it going bad because they are being themselves and performing kinda doesn't make sense as that is what they are suppose to be doing, etc.
4. The achievements were unrealisticall lengthy, which I am sure even the devs noticed with …
